subject: Sliding-window throughput safeguard discussion — Sunburst Medical
messages:
From: Claire Song <claire.song@sunburst-medical.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Sunburst Med Legal <legal@sunburst-medical.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sliding-window throughput safeguard question

Diego —

Thanks for taking this through with the team yesterday. We reviewed the Dedicated capacity proposal and legal has a few follow-ups specifically around the throughput guarantees and queueing behavior for reserved GPUs. Our clinical workloads are latency-sensitive (70% of calls must finish in <200ms for short prompts) and we need clearer language about how Redwood measures and enforces throughput.

Two concrete asks from Sunburst:
- Can Redwood commit to a "sliding-window" throughput guarantee (e.g., 95th percentile of per-second throughput measured on a 60s moving window) rather than a daily/5min average?
- What is the expected behavior when our reservation experiences brief spikes above committed throughput (preemption, admission control, or queueing)? We need an explicit mitigation path and credits schedule if our requests are preempted or delayed.

I've attached a markup of the SLA (Sunburst_SLA_markup.pdf) with comments. Our legal also proposes a temporary higher burst allowance during the first 90 days post-commencement to allow model tuning.

Can you outline what Redwood can do here? If helpful, we can schedule a short call this week.

—Claire
Claire Song
Director of Platform Ops, Sunburst Medical
claire.song@sunburst-medical.com

Attachments: Sunburst_SLA_markup.pdf
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Claire Song <claire.song@sunburst-medical.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sliding-window throughput safeguard question

Claire — thank you, and appreciated the detailed markup. Quick summary from our side and a proposed next step: 

1) Measurement window: We can support a sliding-window style metric. Our engineered default is a 1-minute moving window (per-tenant aggregate TPS / RPS) and we can instrument to produce the 95th percentile over that window. That maps closely to your ask (95th pct over 60s moving windows).

2) Burst behavior & mitigation: For Dedicated, we offer three levers: admission control (reject extra in-flight requests once soft limit reached), short-lived queueing (bounded queue window, default 10s), and preemption to lower-priority workloads. For reserved GPUs we prioritize your in-flight KV caches and we do not evict active sessions under normal operations — however, when cluster-level load forces preemption we fall back to our compatibility model variants (if configured) rather than dropping requests immediately.

3) Credits & escalation: We can add an addendum with a mitigation schedule: credits proportional to the sustained deficit in the sliding-window guarantee (e.g., X% monthly credit for >Y minutes of violations in a month). We typically offer a pilot-level elevated burst allowance (1.5x committed throughput) for the first 60–90 days to allow tuning.

Action: attached a first-pass addendum wording (redwood_proposed_addendum_v1.pdf) that implements a 60s sliding-window 95th percentile metric, a bounded 10s queue with admission control, and a credit schedule. Can you flag areas in your markup you want us to accept/modify? If you're OK with it, let's run a short priority-lane test (30m synthetic spike test) next week.

I can join a call with Ben (Sales) and Lauren (Product) to align on the legal redlines — proposed slots: Wed 07/15 10:00am PT or Thu 07/16 2:00pm PT.

Thanks —
Diego Fernandez
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_proposed_addendum_v1.pdf
From: Claire Song <claire.song@sunburst-medical.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Sunburst Med Legal <legal@sunburst-medical.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sliding-window throughput safeguard question

Diego — thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft. A few notes from legal (high-level) and ops: 

- Legal wants the credit formula to be deterministic and capped (they've suggested a per-minute $ credit up to a monthly cap) and they prefer the metric expressed in tokens/sec with an allowance for model-induced variance.
- Ops requests a slightly longer bounded queue for our mix of short inference + embeddings requests — they'd like 20s queueing instead of 10s for the first 30 days while we test tuning.
- On bursts: legal is amenable to the 60–90 day elevated burst approach but wants explicit guardrails on how burst credits are consumed and a scheduled review at day 30 and day 60.

I've attached our redline (embedded comments in Sunburst_SLA_markup.pdf) and also pasted a small excerpt below: 

> "Sunburst requests a temporary burst allowance of 2.0x committed throughput for the first 60 days, with explicit consumption tracking and a 30-day milestone review to confirm stability. If Redwood elects to queue beyond the bounded window, Sunburst must be notified via escalations channel and receive pro-rated credits."

Happy to review the redwood_proposed_addendum_v1 offline and mark edits. Booking the Wed 07/15 10:00am PT slot now — please confirm attendees.

—Claire

Claire — Ben here (lead for Strategic Sales). I'll join the Wed call and bring the priority-lane test plan. A couple quick notes so we're aligned before the call: 

- We can increase the pilot queue bound to 20s for the initial tuning window and instrument detailed per-minute telemetry so your ops team can see when credits would start to accrue.
- The 2.0x burst ask is material; we can support a 1.8x temporary burst for 60 days with explicit consumption meters and a hard monthly cap. If Sunburst wants 2.0x we need a short operational runbook for priority-lane failover to avoid impacting other tenants.

I'll bring legal on the call if needed. Confirmed attendees from Redwood: Diego, Ben, Lauren, and Kimberly (engineering on the call). See you Wed 10:00am PT.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Claire Song <claire.song@sunburst-medical.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sliding-window throughput safeguard question

Claire — thanks, all. From Product/Engineering perspective:

- We are comfortable committing to a 95th percentile on a 60s sliding window measured in tokens/sec for your primary inference route, with instrumentation and per-minute export to your monitoring stream.
- For the initial 60-day onboarding window we'll accept a 20s bounded queue and a temporary 1.8x burst allowance. We'll include an explicit consumption ledger in the addendum and a 30/60-day operational review cadence.
- Proposed mitigations: if we must queue beyond 20s, we'll route to an isolated compatibility model variant (lower-cost quantized variant) and notify Sunburst via the designated escalation channel; credits will be pro-rated for the minutes impacted.

Diego will push the updated addendum and the priority-lane test plan to the Drive before the call. Thanks everyone — looking forward to locking this down.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Product — Redwood Dedicated
